clue.text: Affair? 28 13 week bachelor is concealing kiss

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside you, so the degree wraps round what follows it

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, the commonest bachelor's degree
28 and 13 together read 'the whole', which is 'all of'
W is the standard abbreviation for week
X is the kiss at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a whole week's fling is something a bachelor keeps hidden, along with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is used for its meaning, not its answer: 'the whole' becomes ALL OF. BA wraps ALL OF plus W, and X follows. The full phrase is 'the whole ball of wax', so it is a theme entry too.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball of wax is American slang for a matter or business, so it can stand for an affair in the sense of a concern.

clue.text: Elements of the Good Book your setter accepts entirely

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the setter's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle signs as Io
the Bible's two parts, the New Testament and the Old Testament, abbreviated NT and OT

explanation.surface: The setter claims to take in every element of the Bible without exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your setter' usually gives I or ME; here it is the setter's pseudonym, Io, split round NT and OT.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for 'in total', used in English to mean completely or as a whole.

clue.text: Menace's dog woman called about kenneling

indicators.note: a kennel houses a dog, so kenneling means holding the woman inside
about here means turned round, so the word for called runs backwards

parts.note: called on the telephone
the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is phoning about boarding the dog belonging to some troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: GNAR, the backward form, kennels SHE. Dennis the Menace is a long-running British comic character in the Beano.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnasher is the wiry-haired pet dog of Dennis the Menace in the Beano comic, so he is literally the Menace's dog.

clue.text: Boy chums working to this degree?

indicators.note: letters that are working are busy moving about, so they are put into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a group of boys working together is the right amount of effort.
explanation.definitionFit: By so much measures an amount of difference, as in 'he won by so much', meaning to this extent; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Even characters spurning dark arts confound it!

indicators.note: spurning the even-numbered letters means throwing out every second one and keeping the odd ones

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Decent people turning their backs on black magic would exclaim in irritation at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adjective meaning steady-tempered; it picks out which letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild oaths of annoyance; drat began as a softened 'God rot', just as confound it softens a curse.

clue.text: Doubly ingenious controls on drugs

indicators.note: doubly tells you to use the next word twice, taking a different part of it each time

parts.note: the final two letters of the word's first use
the opening three letters of its second use

explanation.surface: Two clever regulatory schemes are put in place over narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the word twice, end to end: the join between the copies gives the answer, the end of one plus the start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Using is slang for taking illegal drugs habitually, so a user is someone on drugs.

clue.text: Indifferent cakes crumbled and fed to crow

indicators.note: what is fed to a bird goes inside it, so the jumble goes into the bird's name

parts.note: a jay is a member of the crow family

indicators.note: crumbled food falls apart into bits, so its letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone throws second-rate cakes, crumbled up, to a crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indifferent' looks like a description of the cakes, but it is the definition. The jumble sits between JA and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack-easy is Irish and Scots dialect for not caring either way, so it means unconcerned or offhand.

clue.text: Violin player's equipment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small pocket fiddle once used by dancing masters
second meaning: the gear a sports player uses

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a violinist's gear; the split falls after Violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A kit was a tiny violin carried in the pocket, and kit is also the everyday word for sporting gear and clothing.

clue.text: 27ft square gardens

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three
yard is the American word for a garden

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note on a pair of gardens each twenty-seven feet across.
explanation.walkthrough: '27ft square' reads as one measurement; the definition is just the length. Also a theme entry: the whole nine yards.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is three feet, so nine of them make twenty-seven feet exactly.

clue.text: Women leaving second item at auction house

indicators.note: when someone is leaving they go away, so that letter departs from the phrase

parts.note: items at auction are numbered lots, so the second is lot two
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Some women walk out of a sale room after the second item goes under the hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auction house' reads as one place, but house is the definition: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a numbers game like bingo, which in Britain was long called house or housey-housey.

clue.text: Hospital advances in allaying pain

definitions.note: a noun here, a sudden darting pain

indicators.note: advances means moves forward, so the hospital letter is taken out and put back earlier in the word

parts.note: allaying a pain is easing it
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital makes progress in easing a patient's discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The H moves from fourth place to second. With 27 it also gives the theme phrase 'the whole shooting match'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting is an old noun for a sharp, stabbing sensation, as in shooting pains in the limbs.

clue.text: Small bonus supply from a ewe

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means bendily, so the letters flex into another order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A farmer gets a little extra stock of wool or milk from a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun, as in a store of goods; it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: A few more is a small additional quantity, the sort of modest extra a bonus provides.

clue.text: See 28
Capable of working till?

parts.note: up as in up and running, functioning
until, as in nine to five

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an employee is fit to staff a shop's cash register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like the shop's cash drawer; it is the preposition meaning until.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up to a task is to have the ability for it, so the phrase means equal to or able to do.

clue.text: You shouldn't have disapproval, it's not done

parts.note: what you say on receiving a gift, a thank-you; ta is British informal for thanks
a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone scolds another for doing something socially unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' reads as a rebuke; it is the polite phrase said on receiving a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is something forbidden by custom, which people describe as simply not done.

clue.text: Sean awkwardly over a stage of psychosexual development

indicators.note: over in the sense of covering, so the jumbled name spreads around the letter word
something done awkwardly is clumsy and out of order, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
alpha is the Greek letter a, and alpha also means the first, as a is

explanation.surface: A man named Sean is clumsily getting through one of Freud's developmental phases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the Greek letter's name, alpha, not the article; the jumble wraps it from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freud's theory the anal phase is the second stage of a child's psychosexual growth, after the oral.

clue.text: Our Lady with child in work of stone

indicators.note: a woman with child carries the baby inside her, so one word holds the other

parts.note: Our Lady is the Virgin Mary
a male child

explanation.surface: A carving of the Madonna and Child set in a stone church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With child' means pregnant, which is exactly how the container works.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is building work done in stone or brick by a mason.

clue.text: "Twist Again"? Checker will

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., to twist and strain a joint once more
second meaning: what someone who checks or holds back will do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's Twist Again' was a hit for the singer Chubby Checker, so the surface pairs the song with its singer.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep in check, exactly what a checker does; re-strain is to wrench something a second time.

clue.text: Can it be Basil's top is blown? Violently strike vehicle!

parts.note: can it is slang for be quiet, which is SH

indicators.note: something blown is lost or wasted, so that initial disappears from the verb

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the name
to bang is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Basil Fawlty loses his temper and thrashes his broken-down car, as in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.walkthrough: BE loses its B, leaving E. A theme entry too: the whole shebang.
explanation.definitionFit: Shebang is an old American word for a hut or shack, and the dictionaries also record it for a vehicle or contraption.

clue.text: Washington's corruption finally tempts me in daily

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the word for a cleaner

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in daily
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician confesses that the corruption of the capital tempts them every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb but is the noun for a cleaner. Washington marks the word as American. A theme entry too: the whole schmear.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmear is North American slang for bribery or flattery, so it is US corruption.

clue.text: Without some scruples, sadly

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are wanted, a run lying within them

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone regrets acting with no moral qualms.
explanation.definitionFit: Less as a preposition means minus or lacking, so ten less two is ten without two.

clue.text: Crowd do nothing about cutting chain

indicators.note: what cuts something goes into it, so these letters are set inside the chain

parts.note: an anchor cable is a ship's chain

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the two short words are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
O, zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A gang of idlers loafing about instead of cutting a chain.
explanation.walkthrough: OOD sits inside CABLE. With 8 it gives the theme phrase 'the whole kit and caboodle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle means a collection or lot of people or things, as in the whole caboodle, so a crowd.

clue.text: Spooner's given daiquiri-infused breakfast roll that's unreasonably charged

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an unfair charge

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the two opening sounds trade places

parts.note: a daiquiri is a rum cocktail and a bap is a soft British bread roll; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A bread roll soaked in cocktail, sold at a ridiculous price.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM BAP becomes BUM RAP when the R and B swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bum rap is an American slang term for a false accusation, so something unreasonably charged against a person.

clue.text: Disconcert members of the Hunt?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to unsettle or disturb
second meaning, split in two: a social set who are up, mounted on horseback

explanation.walkthrough: A fox hunt is a mounted British club; its riders are up in the saddle and form a set, and the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to disturb their composure, and the hunt's mounted riders make an up set.

clue.text: Musician's rhythmic activity keeps muscle in range

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a guitarist strums the strings in rhythm
short for pectoral, a chest muscle

explanation.surface: A guitarist's steady playing keeps their muscles within a healthy range of motion.
explanation.walkthrough: A theme entry too: the whole spectrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range of related things, as in a broad spectrum of opinion.

clue.text: Famous contributor to circus businesses

wordplay.note: CO, company, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: A well-known patron supports circus companies.
explanation.walkthrough: Coco the Clown was the stage name of Nicolai Poliakoff, star of the British Bertram Mills Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: Coco the Clown was one of the best-known circus performers of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Light suit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stick you strike for a flame
second meaning: to go well with

explanation.walkthrough: Light suit reads as a summer outfit; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is struck to give light, and colours that match suit each other.

clue.text: Cut through peg, counterintuitively needing e.g. 9, 11 27, 19, 8 & 22, 25, 29, 1 or 20 for completeness

definitions.text: counterintuitively needing e.g. 9, 11 27, 19, 8 & 22, 25, 29, 1 or 20 for completeness

indicators.note: a cut goes through the middle of something, so that word sits inside the peg

parts.note: a thole is a peg in a boat's side that holds the oar
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A woodworker slices through a peg, oddly needing a long list of parts to finish the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The wit is that a phrase meaning everything is itself incomplete without one of the theme entries after it: the whole nine yards, shooting match, shebang, kit and caboodle, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Each listed entry completes an idiom beginning with this phrase, so it needs one of them to make sense.

clue.text: Surrealist hot spots will hold back Kahlo's typical fare?

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in the opposite direction
to hold something is to have it inside, so the spots go around the painter and the temperature letter

parts.note: acne is an outbreak of spots
Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist painter
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A surrealist's lively haunts will withhold Frida Kahlo's usual food.
explanation.walkthrough: ACNE wraps DALIH to give ADALIHCNE, then the lot is reversed. A theme entry too: the whole enchilada.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish, and Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter, so it is food typical of her country.
